records.quote: Lemma 4 (Li and Fang [17]) For two n-dimensional Archimedean copulas C_psi1(u) and C_psi2(u), with phi_2 = psi_2^{-1} = sup{x in R : psi(x) > u} as the right continuous inverse, if phi_2 o psi_1 is super-additive, then C_psi1(u) <= C_psi2(u) for all u in [0,1]^n. Recall that a function f is said to be super-additive if f(x + y) >= f(x) + f(y) for all x and y in the domain of f.
records.family: Archimedean copulas with generators psi_1, psi_2
records.ambiguity: Cited lemma; concordance-type ordering of copulas, not one of the named univariate orders.

a_records.claim: Theorem 20, variant prod p_i >= prod p_i*
a_records.quote: For i = 1, 2, . . . , n, let Ui ~ GM (alpha_i, beta_i, lambda_i) and Vi ~ GM (alpha_i*, beta_i, lambda_i). Further, let Ii (Ii*) be a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of Ui's (Vi's) with E(Ii) = p_i (E(Ii*) = p*_i), i = 1, 2, ..., n. Then, if alpha, alpha* in D+ (E+), beta in D+ and prod_{i=1}^n p_i >= prod_{i=1}^n p*_i,  alpha >=^m alpha* implies X_{1:n} <=hr Y_{1:n}.
